name: Wayback Machine Scraper
description: Wayback Machine scraper for Python and the command line: archived snapshots of a URL or a whole domain with capture time, HTTP status, MIME type, size, content digest and playback links, filtered by date range, as JSON or CSV. Free and open source; sign in with your QuanticData account, no proxies needed.

commands.name: snapshots
commands.help: archived snapshots of a URL or domain
commands.description: Archived snapshots of a URL or domain in the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine: capture time, HTTP status, MIME type, size and content digest, with the playback link and the raw capture link. --match-prefix covers every URL under a path or domain.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: A page URL or a domain, e.g. quantumproxies.io or https://quanticdata.io/docs/.

inputs.name: match_prefix
inputs.description: Match every URL under this path or domain, not just the exact URL.

inputs.name: from
inputs.description: Earliest capture, YYYYMMDD (or a longer timestamp).

inputs.name: newest_first
inputs.description: Return the most recent captures instead of the oldest.

inputs.name: status_code
inputs.description: Only captures with this HTTP status, e.g. 200.

inputs.name: mimetype
inputs.description: Only captures of this MIME type, e.g. text/html.

inputs.name: max_results
inputs.description: How many snapshots to deliver at most (1–1000). You pay only for delivered snapshots.
